greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers us into his one Body, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you reveal to us the mysteries of the Father: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you call us to be faithful stewards of your grace: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you promise us a place at your eternal banquet: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: You will draw water joyfully from the springs of salvation.
homily:
We often think of our lives as a series of rooms we are busy furnishing. We spend so much of our time arranging the furniture of our days—the schedules, the plans, the ambitions, the small details of work and school—that we forget we are not the owners of the house. We are the stewards. We are the ones entrusted with the keys, tasked with keeping the lamps trimmed and the doors unlocked for the Master who is coming. It is a way of living that requires a particular kind of attention, a way of looking at the world that sees beyond the immediate horizon of our own needs.

In the first reading today, St. Paul speaks of a 'stewardship of God’s grace' that was given to him. He describes the mystery of Christ as something that was once hidden but has now been brought to light. Think of that image: a mystery, a treasure, hidden in the heart of God for ages, now revealed for our benefit. Paul calls himself the 'least of all the holy ones,' yet he is entrusted with the 'inscrutable riches of Christ.' He is not a master; he is a servant who has been given something precious to share. He is a man who knows that his life is not his own, but a vessel for a grace that is meant to flow out into the world.

Benjamin Vo lived with this kind of intuitive, gentle stewardship. Think of the way he looked at the world—not as a place to be conquered, but as a place to be explored and shared. He was a boy of brilliant mind, yes, a boy who could navigate the complexities of cloud infrastructure and high-level logic with the ease of someone who felt right at home in the digital architecture of the future. But even more than his intellect, there was that quiet, constant curiosity. He loved the sky. He loved the mechanics of flight. He loved the idea of 'con chim airlines'—not because he wanted to own a fleet of planes, but because he saw in them a way to bridge the distance, a way to connect people, a way to make the world smaller and more hospitable.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has felt like a room that has been locked. You look at the spaces where Ben used to be—the desk where he coded his games, the chair where he sat as he talked about his latest project—and you feel the weight of the stewardship you were given. You were the ones who held the keys to his childhood, the ones who fostered his joy, the ones who provided the love that allowed him to grow into the gentle, radiant soul he was. And I want you to know this: you did not miss a single beat. You were the perfect parents for Benjamin. You were the ones who taught him how to love, how to dream, and how to reach out to others. That stewardship was not a task you finished; it is a bond that is now forever held in the heart of God.

There is a temptation, when we are grieving, to look back and wonder if we were 'prudent' enough, as the Gospel asks us to be. We wonder if we were watching the door closely enough, if we were prepared for the hour that came. Please, let that heavy stone fall from your hearts. You were faithful. You were present. You loved him with a devotion that was, in itself, a reflection of the Father’s love for him. You are not being asked to account for his departure; you are being invited to rest in the fact that he is safe. He is not in the hands of the world anymore; he is in the hands of the One who entrusted him to you in the first place. You are a family of four, and that is a reality that exists beyond the reach of time or distance.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the geometry of this love better than anyone. You know that the bond you share with Ben is not a matter of geography. It is a matter of the heart. When you look at the planes, when you think of the games you coded together, when you feel the quiet of the house, know that you are a vital part of this living mystery. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity. You are the one who knows what it means to be a brother, to be a friend, to be a witness to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who sees the beauty in the small things. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than any distance, that it is the most beautiful material in the universe.

Look at the Gospel again. Jesus tells us to be the 'faithful and prudent steward.' He speaks of a master who returns to find his servants ready. But notice how Jesus describes the reward: 'Truly, I say to you, he will put him in charge of all his property.' The Master does not just take back the keys; he gives us more. He invites us into the full inheritance of the Kingdom. All the longing, all the 'what ifs,' all the quiet moments of missing him—they are all leading to this moment. They are leading to the banquet where the table is set, where the divide is gone, and where we will be reunited with the ones we love in the presence of the One who loves us most. Ben is already at that table. He is already in the place where the light never fades, where the curiosity is satisfied, and where the joy is complete.

We are living in a time that often feels like a house in the middle of the night—dark, quiet, and sometimes disorienting. We see the world changing, we feel the ground shifting, and we are tempted to look for security in the things we can build ourselves. But Jesus is inviting us to look at the Master. He is inviting us to look at the One who holds the keys to the future. He is inviting us to trust that the house is sound, that the foundation is deep, and that the Architect knows exactly what he is doing. You are not a random collection of moments. You are a masterpiece in progress. You are a dwelling place for the Spirit.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is not a new set of plans. It is a simple, quiet, doable thing: keep your lamp lit. When you feel the weight of the silence, when you feel the ache of the absence, choose to light the lamp of hope. Choose to do one small act of kindness in Ben’s name, just as you have done with the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a sign, a tangible, physical piece of the mystery that you are living. It is a sign that the love that was poured into Ben is still flowing, still quenching the thirst of the poor, still bringing life to the dry places. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope, you are adding a stone to the temple. You are making the structure stronger. You are keeping the light burning.

Do not be afraid of the ache. It is the price of loving well. It is the mark of a heart that is truly alive. And do not be afraid of the silence. It is not a void; it is a space where God is waiting to serve you. If you listen, if you really listen, you will hear the voice of the Father calling you by name, just as he called Benjamin. You will hear the promise that you are a family of four, forever. You will hear the invitation to keep walking, to keep hoping, to keep trusting. The road is long, and it is sometimes steep, but you are not walking it alone. You are being held by the same hands that hold the universe. You are being loved with a love that has no end. And one day, the journey will reach its destination, and you will understand everything. You will see that every step, every tear, every moment of longing was part of the way home.

Keep your eyes on the horizon. Keep your heart in the light. And remember that he is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the banquet is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may his face shine upon you forever. Go in peace, trusting in the promise of the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace.
For all families who carry the weight of grief, that God may console them with his presence and fill their hearts with the hope of eternal reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
You have heard of the stewardship of God’s grace
that was given to me for your benefit,
namely, that the mystery was made known to me by revelation,
as I have written briefly earlier.
When you read this
you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ,
which was not made known to human beings in other generations
as it has now been revealed
to his holy Apostles and prophets by the Spirit,
that the Gentiles are coheirs, members of the same Body,
and copartners in the promise in Christ Jesus through the Gospel.Of this I became a minister by the gift of God’s grace
that was granted me in accord with the exercise of his power.
To me, the very least of all the holy ones, this grace was given,
to preach to the Gentiles the inscrutable riches of Christ,
and to bring to light for all what is the plan of the mystery
hidden from ages past in God who created all things,
so that the manifold wisdom of God
might now be made known through the Church
to the principalities and authorities in the heavens.
This was according to the eternal purpose
that he accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
in whom we have boldness of speech
and confidence of access through faith in him.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (see 3)  You will draw water joyfully from the springs of salvation.
God indeed is my savior;
I am confident and unafraid.
My strength and my courage is the LORD,
and he has been my savior.
With joy you will draw water
at the fountain of salvation.
R. You will draw water joyfully from the springs of salvation.
Give thanks to the LORD, acclaim his name;
among the nations make known his deeds,
proclaim how exalted is his name.
R. You will draw water joyfully from the springs of salvation.
Sing praise to the LORD for his glorious achievement;
let this be known throughout all the earth.
Shout with exultation, O city of Zion,
for great in your midst
is the Holy One of Israel!
R. You will draw water joyfully from the springs of salvation.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples: 
“Be sure of this:
if the master of the house had known the hour
when the thief was coming,
he would not have let his house be broken into.
You also must be prepared,
for at an hour you do not expect, the Son of Man will come.”Then Peter said,
“Lord, is this parable meant for us or for everyone?”
And the Lord replied,
“Who, then, is the faithful and prudent steward
whom the master will put in charge of his servants
to distribute the food allowance at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master on arrival finds doing so.
Truly, I say to you, he will put him
in charge of all his property.
But if that servant says to himself,
‘My master is delayed in coming,’
and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants,
to eat and drink and get drunk,
then that servant’s master will come
on an unexpected day and at an unknown hour
and will punish the servant severely
and assign him a place with the unfaithful.
That servant who knew his master’s will
but did not make preparations nor act in accord with his will
shall be beaten severely;
and the servant who was ignorant of his master’s will
but acted in a way deserving of a severe beating
shall be beaten only lightly. 
Much will be required of the person entrusted with much,
and still more will be demanded of the person entrusted with more.”

day: Wednesday of the Twenty-ninth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!
